ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, block $A$, rectangular object $B$ with a smooth fixed pulley, and the hanging small ball $C$ are in a state of rest. The contact surfaces between $A$ and $B$, and between $B$ and the ground are both rough. The light rope and light spring that pass over the smooth fixed pulley are connected to the small ball $C$, respectively. The central axis of the light spring makes an angle of $60^{\circ}$ with the vertical direction, and the light rope makes an angle of $30^{\circ}$ with the vertical direction. The masses of $A$, $B$, and $C$ are $m_{A}=2\mathrm{kg}$, $m_{B}=5\mathrm{kg}$, and $m_{C}=1\mathrm{kg}$, respectively. The elongation of the spring is $\Delta x=2\mathrm{cm}$ (the gravitational acceleration $g$ is taken as $10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$).

1. The spring constant $k$
2. The static friction force exerted by object $B$ on block $A$
3. The frictional force exerted by the ground on object $B$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
$250\mathrm{N/m}$
$5\sqrt{3}\mathrm{N}$, direction horizontally to the right
$\frac{5\sqrt{3}}{2}\mathrm{N}$, direction horizontally to the right

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, on the left is a fixed wall, and a light spring extends obliquely downward to the right from the left wall to connect to small ball C; the spring axis is marked as 60° with the vertical direction. Small ball C is also connected by a section of light rope obliquely upward to the right to a smooth fixed pulley fixed above the upper left of object B, and the oblique rope is marked as 30° with the vertical dashed line. After passing around the pulley, the rope extends horizontally to the right and connects to block A placed on the upper surface of B. The large rectangular object B is placed on a rough horizontal ground, and the contact surface between A and B is also rough; the whole is at rest. Reasoning: Let the spring tension be F and the tension in the rope be T. For force equilibrium of small ball C: in the horizontal direction, the horizontal component of the upper-right rope tension equals the horizontal component of the upper-left spring tension, so T sin30° = F sin60°; in the vertical direction, the sum of the vertical components of the two tensions equals the weight, so T cos30° + F cos60° = m_C g = 1×10 = 10 N. From T sin30° = F sin60°, obtain T/2 = (√3/2)F, namely T = √3 F. Substituting into the vertical equation: (√3F)(√3/2) + F(1/2) = 10, namely 3F/2 + F/2 = 10, therefore 2F = 10, F = 5 N. Therefore the spring stiffness coefficient k = F/Delta x = 5/0.02 = 250 N/m; the rope tension T = 5√3 N. For block A: the horizontal rope segment pulls A toward the pulley, namely pulls it to the left, with magnitude T. A is at rest, so the static friction force of B on A must be equal in magnitude and opposite in direction to the rope tension, namely f_{B on A}=T=5√3 N, in the horizontal direction to the right. Analyze object B together with its fixed pulley but not including A in the horizontal direction: the friction force of A on B is opposite to the friction force of B on A, with magnitude 5√3 N and direction to the left. The rope has two sections of tension on the pulley: the horizontal rope segment pulls the pulley to the right with T; the oblique rope segment pulls obliquely downward to the left along the rope, and its horizontal component is T sin30° = T/2 to the left. Therefore the resultant horizontal action of the rope on the pulley is T - T/2 = T/2 to the right. Except for ground friction, the horizontal resultant force on B is T/2 to the right and T to the left, net T/2 to the left. To remain at rest, the friction force of the ground on B should be T/2 to the right, namely (5√3)/2 N to the right.
